purpose: Mirabegron is used to treat overactive bladder, which causes sudden urges to urinate, leaking urine, or needing to go to the bathroom very often. It helps reduce those embarrassing urges and accidents. It can also be used in children for certain bladder conditions.
how_it_works: Your bladder has special receptors on it, kind of like little switches. Mirabegron flips a switch called the beta-3 receptor, which tells the bladder muscles to relax and hold more urine. This means your bladder does not squeeze as suddenly or as often, giving you more control.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include high blood pressure, a stuffy or runny nose, urinary tract infections, and headache. Some people also notice a faster heartbeat or back pain. These are usually mild.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have high blood pressure, kidney problems, or liver problems, as your dose may need to be adjusted. Mirabegron can raise blood pressure, so your blood pressure should be checked regularly. It can also interact with other medications, so always tell your pharmacist about everything else you take. Do not take it if you are allergic to any of its ingredients.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose for adults is 25 mg taken by mouth once a day with or without food. After about 8 weeks, your doctor may increase your dose to 50 mg once a day if needed. Swallow the tablet whole — do not crush or chew it.
